chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'shah) from Safwan from Muthanna from Karib al-Sayrafi said:

We were all together, so we bought a bird, plucked it, and brought it into the Haram (sanctuary). Our companions, the people of Mecca, criticized that for us. So Karib sent to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him, and he said: 'Entrust it to a Muslim man from the people of Mecca or a woman. When its feathers have fully regrown, they will clear its path (allow it to fly free).'
And it is not permissible to hunt any of the pigeons of the Haram, even if they are in the Ihlat (open land outside the sanctuary). He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a bird brought into the Haram by mistake, and are Haram pigeons protected from hunting?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of *kaffarah* (expiation) for minor Ihram violations, specifically highlighting the juristic distinction between the sanctity of the Haram's airspace and its ground. The ruling to entrust the bird to a local resident reflects the scholarly principle of preserving the bird's life while respecting the prohibition on hunting within the sacred precincts. It further clarifies that the protection of Haram birds extends to their movements outside the boundary, a point of nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the scope of *haram* restrictions.
